Compress Image to 500KB

At 500KB most photos keep high quality. This is useful for email attachments and larger upload limits.

Compression tool

Target size Target size:
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

High-quality results

The tool will often keep your full dimensions at this target and only lower JPEG or WebP quality.

PNG at 500KB

Screenshots and graphics saved as PNG can often fit 500KB, which is a more realistic PNG target than 20KB.

A high-quality target

Five hundred kilobytes is 512,000 bytes. At this size, most photographs retain strong detail and smooth gradients. It is useful when a portal allows half a megabyte, when you need to email several pictures, or when you want to shrink very large photos without visible loss for everyday viewing.

Phone photos are often between two and eight megabytes, so reaching 500KB can mean a big saving even though the image still looks nearly the same on a normal screen.

What changes and what stays

The tool tries to keep your original dimensions and lowers JPEG or WebP quality only as much as needed. If dimensions must change, you will see the final size on the result card. Very high-resolution scans or panoramic photos may still need a modest resize.

If you plan to print an image, keep a higher target or the original, because print needs more pixels than a screen.

Using PNG at 500KB

This is the first target where PNG becomes realistic for many graphics. Logos, charts and interface screenshots often fit inside 500KB as PNG with no quality loss. Photographs still usually favour JPEG or WebP.

Tips for email and messaging

Many email systems limit total message size, not just one attachment, so compress each photo and check the total. Remember that attachments are often encoded in a way that makes them somewhat larger in transit. Leaving some headroom is wise.

Examples where 500KB works well

A wedding or travel photo of several megabytes can usually reach 500KB with little visible change on a phone or laptop screen. A product photo for an online shop, shown at about 1,200 pixels wide, normally fits comfortably. Large infographics may need PNG or WebP to keep text sharp.

For galleries, compress each image separately and keep the originals in a safe folder so that you can re-export at a different size later.

When you need more than 500KB

If the picture is for print, large displays or detailed editing, do not compress it to 500KB. Use the custom size box to choose a larger target, up to 10,240 KB, or keep the original. Compression is a trade-off, and for some jobs the original is the right file.

Check, then download

After processing, compare the previews and look at fine detail such as text, hair and edges. The result card lists original and final size, the percentage saved and the final dimensions. Download singly or as a ZIP when you have processed several images.

Compression and color accuracy

Strong compression can shift subtle colors and flatten gradients such as skies. At 500KB these effects are usually small, but if color accuracy matters, for example for product photos, compare the preview against the original on a good screen. JPEG converts pictures to the sRGB look most screens use, so a photo with a wide-gamut profile may look slightly different afterwards. For critical work, keep the original and use the compressed copy only for sharing.

Common questions

Will the image keep its dimensions?

Often yes, unless the target needs a resize. The result panel shows final dimensions.
